_comment: Declarative catalogue of the firmware images this project analyses.
Vendor firmware is NOT redistributed in this repository. This file plus
tools/fetch-firmware.sh lets any reader obtain byte-identical images and
verify them, which is what actually matters for reproducing a result.
'expected' hashes marked null are pinned on first successful fetch; see
firmware/MANIFEST.json for the recorded values and fetch timestamps.
2026-08-18: three images were added that are NOT this device's firmware -
two N300RT and one N200RE. They carry a `model` field for that reason and
the `device` block above still describes the one unit this project owns.
They are here because register rows need them: P8-21 names N300RT in its
refutation condition, and the N200RE build is the closest publicly
downloadable point in time to the build this unit actually runs. A claim
derived from one of them is a claim about an image, never about hardware

device.soc_expected: Realtek RTL8196x (to be confirmed empirically - see notes/anatomy-n150rt.md)

why: Predates the December 2019 Realtek-SDK disclosure by four years.
Expected to contain the vulnerable code paths in their original form,
which makes it the reference point for root-cause analysis.

sources.note: Internet Archive item TOTOLINKN150RTV2.1.2B20150825.1601; hashes below come from the item metadata API, so they are verifiable independently of the download.

notes: The r6cr section header declares a payload length that runs 9 bytes
past the end of this file. Either the archived copy is slightly
truncated or the length field covers a trailer this copy lacks.
Extraction is unaffected - the SquashFS image itself is complete and
unpacks cleanly - but a second source should be compared before the
container format is documented as final.

why: Built 2020-10-30, i.e. nine months AFTER the 2020-01-23 full disclosure
The advisory lists 'N150RT through 3.4.0' as affected, so this build sits
exactly on the boundary. Diffing it against 2.1.2 answers a question the
CVE records do not: did the vendor actually remove the config.dat dump and
the formSysCmd handler, or only the syscmd.htm UI page that exposed it?

images.role: sibling model - the only image here that is not an N150RT, and the reason it is here is a register row, not curiosity
why: P8-21 asks whether the six products CVE-2024-51228 names are one codebase or six, and its frozen refutation is literally 'obtain another model's image and find a different dispatch table'. N300RT is one of the six. Until 2026-08-18 that row sat on the bench list, where it did not belong: it needs an image, not a router.

It is also the same product version this unit reports (V2.1.6) at the published build B20160516, which is the build the N150RT V2.1.6 entry under `wanted` is a 40%-complete download of. Different model, so it does NOT close that gap - but it is a complete 2016 V2.1.6 of this SDK family, which nothing else here is.

sources.note: Third-party firmware mirror; the same one the V3.4.0 entry above came from. TOTOLINK publishes no signature, so these hashes assert continuity and never authenticity: they say two people fetched the same bytes, not that TOTOLINK produced them. Fetched in a browser on 2026-08-18 - the Zone.Identifier alternate data stream the OS wrote at download time is on disk beside each file. If the mirror serves different bytes later that is a signal to investigate, not a reason to re-pin.

notes: Container starts with a w6cg section (77 36 63 67), i.e. the 2015-family layout this unit also has, rather than the cr6c-first layout of V3.4.0.
No claim is made here about N300RT hardware. This project owns one N150RT; everything derived from this image is a statement about an image.

images.role: nearest-in-time publicly downloadable build to the one this unit runs
why: This unit runs TOTOLINK-CX-N150RT-V2.1.6-B20171121.1002, which is on no download page. Every boa finding in this repository is therefore measured either on a 2015 image, on a 2020 image, or on a build nobody else can obtain - and the last of those is the one that matters and the one that cannot be reproduced.

B20180330 is four months later than B20171121 and is downloadable. It does not make this unit's build reproducible; it makes it possible to ask whether a defect found here also stands in a 2018-era image a reader can fetch, which is the difference between a finding somebody can check and one they have to take on trust.

Two rows want this specifically: bughunt.md #5 (the supervisor credential pair, currently bounded to 2015 and to this unit) and #20 (the 601-second IP session arm, currently read only in this unit's binary).

images.role: a date, not a defect - it brackets when the vendor changed the authentication path
why: uninit-credential-pair.md establishes that the second, never-written credential comparison is present in 2015 and in this unit's 2018 build and absent from V3.4.0-B20201030. That places the change somewhere in a five-year window, which is not a timeline.

A V3.4.0 built 2019-03-15 splits that window. Whichever way it comes out is informative: present means the removal is late and deliberate, absent means it happened before this build and the 2020 image is not where to look.

Same-version different-model, so a difference between this and N150RT-V3.4.0-B20201030 is a difference in EITHER date OR model and the two are not separable from these two files alone. Anything concluded from it has to say so.

wanted.status: INCOMPLETE - do not analyse as if whole
why: This unit's /etc/version reads TOTOLINK-CX-N150RT-V2.1.6-B20171121.1002.
The published V2.1.6 is build B20160516 - the same product version, a different
build, eighteen months earlier. So W02's 'the resident build is on no download
page' survives, with better precision: the VERSION is published, this BUILD is not.
Completing this download would let a reader reproduce a third point on the vendor
remediation timeline without owning the hardware.

sources.note: Downloaded in a browser on 2026-08-16; the two URLs above are not typed from memory, they are read out of the file's Windows Zone.Identifier alternate data stream, which the operating system wrote at download time. That is provenance evidence rather than recollection. Softpedia is a third-party mirror: the vendor publishes no signature, so a hash asserts only that two people fetched the same bytes, never that TOTOLINK produced them.

observed.completeness: 40.3% of the compressed stream; there is no central directory, so unzip rejects the file outright - which reads as corrupt and means truncated
observed.recovered_crc32: 0xb051aa45 - MISMATCH against the stored value, as it must be while the file is short. Recorded so the number is not mistaken for a passing check.
observed.recovery: tools/zipprefix.py; deflate is a stream, so the prefix decompresses. Three independent derivations agree byte-for-byte on the same sha256.

partial_evidence.note: Two of the three sections are BYTE-COMPLETE, not merely headed. An earlier version of this entry said 'section lengths only', which understated the artefact by a whole section. What is missing is the rootfs, and therefore /etc/version, boa and root_form[].
partial_evidence.w6cg: flash 0x010000, 296,804 declared and 296,804 present - COMPLETE, bzip2
partial_evidence.cr6c: flash 0x060000, ram 0x80500000, 986,114 declared and 986,114 present - COMPLETE; inner lzma-alone at +0x2808 decompresses to 3,374,608 bytes reaching end-of-stream
partial_evidence.r6cr: truncated - this is the only part that needs the other 60%
partial_evidence.kernel_self_identification: Linux version 2.6.30.9 (acer1@localhost.localdomain) (gcc 4.4.5) #1338 Thu May 12 21:05, cmdline 'console=ttyS0,38400 root=/dev/mtdblock1'

provenance_strength.withdrawn: An earlier version argued that the kernel section lengths 985,090 -> 986,114 -> 987,138 are 'exactly 1,024 bytes apart at each step, and a tampered file does not land on that line'. That is wrong. Adding the 2020 build shows all four are 962/963/964/1206 times 1024, PLUS 2 - the section is padded to a 1 KiB grid, so the spacing is the container format and not a property of these files. Exactly one grid point lies between the 2015 and 2018 values, so a correctly built kernel of that size lands on it by construction.
provenance_strength.weak_but_real: w6cg is NOT on the grid (remainders 642 / 868 / 532) and does fall between its neighbours: 308,866 -> 296,804 -> 277,012. An ordering test across a ~32 KiB window.
stronger: The DOS timestamp in the local file header (2016-05-16 12:34:30) is a different field from the filename's B20160516 text. A mirror can type a filename; the timestamp is written by the packer.

Inside the COMPRESSED kernel, where renaming cannot reach: a build banner dated Thu May 12, four days before the archive timestamp, and a console baud rate that matches the 26us bit time measured on this hardware in W02.
provenance_strength.ceiling: Unchanged and low. TOTOLINK publishes no signature, so none of the above shows these bytes came from the vendor. It raises the cost of a forgery from renaming a file to rebuilding a kernel, and no further.

wanted.next: Re-download in a browser. The success criterion is fixed in advance: tools/zipprefix.py must report CRC-32 == 0xd20c0622 and exit zero. Only then compare /etc/version, root_form[] and the sink census against unit-2018.
